# Combat Rogue — what the bots run

**Recommendation (what the bots run).** Endgame build (level 60), 20/31/0 — respec at level 40. The decision loop walks 92 rules in ascending priority and executes the first whose condition is true. The party fixtures place this spec on level 38 (1 member), level 48 (2 members). [measured on bot runs, private 1.18.1-based realm — `knowledge/classes/rogue/combat/talents.yaml`, `rotation.yaml`]

**Measured in round 155** (amp-6's per-spec table). No measured numbers for this spec: it has no row in the round-155 table, which lists the 14 specs with boss-fight data [measured].

**This page is the bots' half.** It records what our party bots actually run for this spec — the level-60 build and the level-by-level order, the rule firing order the decision loop walks, the kit bands, the round-155 measurement and the recorded deviations. The hand-written guide for this spec is [combat.md](./combat.md).

## How the bots play it

On every decision tick the loop walks the rules in ascending `priority`, executes the first one whose condition is true and skips the rest of that tick. The groups below are a reading aid; the priority numbers are the real order. Level is the rule's own `level_min` — the first level it can fire.

### Single target

- **60 — Riposte** (`RC06-riposte`) — level 20+ · intent `filler` · spell 14251
  - **When:** the target is hostile; in melee range; the resident has the block/dodge/parry state; Riposte is off cooldown; at least 10 energy; the target does not have Gouge.
  - **Why:** Combat talent (115) at 20, DependsOn Deflection 5/5, which is why 112 is the second five points.
  - Sources: [measured on bot runs, private 1.18.1-based realm — `knowledge/classes/rogue/combat/rotation.yaml`; supporting: `DBC Talent.dbc:115`; `sql tw_world_spell_template.sql L10954`; `DBC SpellCastTimes.dbc:1`; +5 more].

  - **When:** the target is hostile; in melee range; the resident has the aura state 14 state; at least 10 energy; at most 80 energy; the target does not have Gouge.
  - **Why:** Turtle content: a Combat talent (122) at 30, 10 energy, casterAuraState 14 -- AURA_STATE_TARGET_DODGED, which the core sets on a rogue whose attack the target dodged.

## Situational notes from the rule notes

Every sentence below is copied from a rule's own note (the rule id is in front of it) and mentions a situation the rule exists for. Rest, food and drink rules are left out here; their items are in the band table above.

- **RC00u-mongoose — Use Elixir of the Mongoose:** HO-TKB-PLAY-205 (PIONEER FIX, orchestrator for the owner full-kit order 2026-10-18: buff food, elixirs, oils and stones in use): Elixir of the Mongoose (item 13452, required level 46), elixir or potion (aura 17538 while it lasts), out of combat, not moving, not eating or drinking, only when the bags hold it and the buff or enchant is missing (or under 5 min for an enchant), so it is also re-applied after a death or a swap. The spec's own guide page names it (line 242); the item and its aura or enchant id are read from the DB (docs/research/db-queries/tkbplay-205.result.txt).

- **RC01-stealth — Stealth:** HO-P4-GROUP-274 (round 117, play-client next to Ivo, a combat rogue of 20 travelling the Barrens road: Stealth (1785) was cast at 00:04:09Z mid-walk because a mob stood within 30 yd; the server slowed him to 4.2 yd/s and re-sent his path, the watcher, 20 yd off and not detecting him, never got that path and drew the old 7 yd/s one for 151 s, then saw him reappear 600 yd back): NOT WHILE MOVING. A player stealths when he stops to open on something, not on the road.
- **RC02b-vanish — Vanish:** At the pin Vanish 1856 is spellLevel 22, trainer-taught, 300 s category cooldown; effect 79 (EffectSanctuary) calls InterruptAttacksOnMe and DoResetThreat, and 1856 carries no aura 16 of its own, so the module's grouped-stealth refusal does not refuse it. HO-TKB-PLAY-174 (PIONEER FIX, observer Hateforge playbook section 1.5, p4-group 456 core-script read L296-L339, vocabulary v35 enemies_engaged_entry): never while Har'gesh Doomcaller (60737) has a Faceless Terror (60738) alive: a Terror with no victim calls the boss EnterEvadeMode every 5 s, which resets him to full health and despawns the Terrors, and an evade by a hunter or rogue leaves the Terror victimless.
- **RC03-adrenaline-rush — Adrenaline Rush:** "Pop it once on the pull if the boss dies within ~3 minutes, twice on longer fights" (combat.md L125, L153: the 180 s recoveryTime lets the rule fire again on a long fight); "rogues can pull aggro when they pop cooldowns at the start of a fight. Only on a boss of the dungeon plan (`target.boss`): the guide names bosses and fights, not trash.
- **RC04-blade-flurry — Blade Flurry:** 25 energy, 4 s recoveryTime, and its three aura effects are haste and an extra target, so it is only worth its global with a second enemy inside 8 yd.
- **RC04c-blade-flurry-off — Cancel Blade Flurry:** "1 target: Blade Flurry off; it lowers your single-target damage" (combat.md L141, L28); the spell text says damage and energy regeneration are reduced while it is active and it lasts until cancelled (tkbplay-230.result.txt: aura 110, durationIndex 21, 4 s recoveryTime). RC04 turns it on with two or more hostiles within 8 yd and nothing turned it off again, so the aura stayed up (89 to 97 per cent of combat ticks on the four pioneer combat rogues, RC00's note, HO-TKB-PLAY-165).
- **RC05-kick-t1 — Kick:** Same when and same spell; the view takes only a caster whose interruptible cast is one of the listed ids, so the kick goes to a heal, then a fear, charm, polymorph, stun or sleep, then a summon or channel, then the nearest caster (the plain rule, which keeps nukes and fillers). 193 adds the Atal'ai camp casts the boss rows lack: Heal 11642, Sleep 12098, Summon 12151 (DB, docs/research/db-queries/tkbplay-192.result.txt).
- **RC05-kick-t2 — Kick:** HO-TKB-PLAY-192 and 193 (PIONEER FIX, orchestrator, p1-loop v41 casting list): the ranked version of RC05-kick, tier 2 of 3 (rank 2, fears, charms, polymorphs, stuns and sleeps; 14 ids). Same when and same spell; the view takes only a caster whose interruptible cast is one of the listed ids, so the kick goes to a heal, then a fear, charm, polymorph, stun or sleep, then a summon or channel, then the nearest caster (the plain rule, which keeps nukes and fillers).
- **RC05-kick-t3 — Kick:** HO-TKB-PLAY-192 and 193 (PIONEER FIX, orchestrator, p1-loop v41 casting list): the ranked version of RC05-kick, tier 3 of 3 (rank 2, summons and interruptible channels; 14 ids). Same when and same spell; the view takes only a caster whose interruptible cast is one of the listed ids, so the kick goes to a heal, then a fear, charm, polymorph, stun or sleep, then a summon or channel, then the nearest caster (the plain rule, which keeps nukes and fillers).
- **RC05-kick — Kick:** The interrupt: 25 energy, 10 s categoryRecoveryTime, spent on a cast rather than on cooldown. A bot only interrupted the mob it had selected, so with the party on another mob nobody stopped the heal or the cast (Jammal'an's Healing Wave, the Hateforge cleric's Greater Heal).
- **RC06-riposte — Riposte:** 10 energy, 6 s recoveryTime, and it carries casterAuraState 1 -- AURA_STATE_DEFENSE, the state the core sets after the rogue blocks, dodges or parries -- so the core refuses the cast outright without it. HO-TKB-PLAY-011 (decision 62, Riposte notes): CORRECTION (tkb-refresh finding, decision 62): at the pin a rogues DODGE does not set AURA_STATE_DEFENSE; Unit.cpp skips it for CLASS_ROGUE ("skip Rogue Riposte"), and only a parry (or block) does.
- **RC02f-flourish — Flourish:** HO-TKB-PLAY-261 (leveller pass, brackets 40-59): Flourish (45604, trainer level 42, 20 energy, 40 s cooldown, stances 0, a finisher: +20% parry for 8 s at one combo point to 16 s at five, aura 45604 on the rogue; `doc research/db-queries/tkbplay-261.result.txt`).
- **RC07-surprise-attack — Surprise Attack:** Turtle content: a Combat talent (122) at 30, 10 energy, casterAuraState 14 -- AURA_STATE_TARGET_DODGED, which the core sets on a rogue whose attack the target dodged.
- **RC08-gouge — Gouge:** HO-TKB-PLAY-028 (orchestrator, levelling window): Gouge is broken by any damage (AuraInterruptFlags 2, removed on damage taken) and this rule used to fire on the ONLY target and be broken by the very next push: Vessia (Assassination, level 10, solo) Gouged at hp < 30 on her one mob and Sinister Strike followed 1-4 s later, twice (stream 20.jsonl 13:41:13 and 13:42:05). HO-TKB-PLAY-029 (orchestrator, vocabulary v10): the archive uses it on a SECOND mob ("If a second mob joins, Gouge one and kill the other", "If both are on you, Gouge one, then Evasion"), and `target: other_engaged` now aims it there: the nearest living hostile attacking the rogue that is not the kill target, read through its own health, auras and melee reach.
- **RC10k-kidney-shot-runner — Kidney Shot:** HO-TKB-PLAY-095 (orchestrator rank 3, round 106): Kidney Shot (spell 408, level 30, 20 energy, a combo-point stun finisher on a 20 s cooldown) ALONE, on a fleeing mob or an elite with three or more combo points: the guide calls it the stun finisher for dangerous mobs (rogue/leveling.md L95, L167, L184). The second attacker cannot be the target (the combo points are on the main target; `target: other_engaged` would aim a finisher at a mob with none), so the rule is the runner and the elite.
- **RC09-slice-and-dice — Slice and Dice:** `combo_on_target` carries the archive's other warning about the same resource -- "Do not apply a combo-point builder to an add; it wipes the boss's combo points (combo points persist per target since CC2, but only within a single target's pool)".
- **RC10-eviscerate — Eviscerate:** 30 energy, direct damage, no duration to lose, so it is gated on the target being nearly dead rather than on an aura.
- **RC10a-cheap-shot — Cheap Shot:** HO-TKB-PLAY-134 (orchestrator, round 123 rogue read: 37 of 67 L25+ deaths followed a Vanish, a median 10 s later, 6 of them reopened by Cheap Shot or Ambush at low health): a stealth opener waits for 50 per cent health, so a Vanished rogue does not reopen the fight it fled. HO-TKB-PLAY-011 (decision 62, ROG-05): the solo opener from Stealth, placed directly above the first builder.
- **RC10b-ambush — Ambush:** HO-TKB-PLAY-134 (orchestrator, round 123 rogue read: 37 of 67 L25+ deaths followed a Vanish, a median 10 s later, 6 of them reopened by Cheap Shot or Ambush at low health): a stealth opener waits for 50 per cent health, so a Vanished rogue does not reopen the fight it fled. HO-TKB-PLAY-027 (decision 86, OQ-1807): the stealth opener from behind.
- **RC10c-garrote — Garrote:** HO-TKB-PLAY-134 (orchestrator, round 123 rogue read: 37 of 67 L25+ deaths followed a Vanish, a median 10 s later, 6 of them reopened by Cheap Shot or Ambush at low health): a stealth opener waits for 50 per cent health, so a Vanished rogue does not reopen the fight it fled. HO-TKB-PLAY-027 (decision 86, OQ-1807): Garrote 703 is spellLevel 14, 50 energy, Stealth required, no weapon requirement, behind-only at the pin: the opener a rogue without a dagger still has from behind.
- **RC11-ghostly-strike — Ghostly Strike:** HO-TKB-PLAY-134 (orchestrator, round 123 rogue read - 37 of 67 L25+ deaths followed a Vanish, a median 10 s later, 6 of them reopened by Cheap Shot or Ambush at low health) - out of combat under 50 per cent health the rogue does not start a fight (it would break the Vanish stealth as the opener would); in a fight nothing changes.

## What the bots do not do (from the rule notes)

Sentences from the rules' notes that say what is deliberately not implemented, or that name an open question.

- **RC00w-dissolvent-ii-main:** The guide's Deadly V and Corrosive II are AQ20 items and are not built; Deadly and Corrosive on bosses is contested for Combat Envenom in the guide and is not built either.
- **RC00x-dissolvent-ii-off:** The guide's Deadly V and Corrosive II are AQ20 items and are not built; Deadly and Corrosive on bosses is contested for Combat Envenom in the guide and is not built either.
- **RC03-adrenaline-rush:** NOT built, and why: the guide times AR 'right after a 5-point Rupture, so its Backstabs happen inside the Taste for Blood window' (L125), but the build HO-TKB-PLAY-211 gave (Assassination 20: no Taste for Blood, no Rupture) has neither, and the guide itself says Rupture is worse than Eviscerate without Taste for Blood (leveling.md L96, L98); so the Rupture-to-Adrenaline-Rush sequencing is an open question in the handoff.
- **RC02f-flourish:** NOT built: "Whirlwind-style attacks" (no term for a mob's area attack) and the tank-niche "overlap Ghostly Strike with Flourish" (L187: a rogue is not a dungeon tank in our population).
- **RC10-eviscerate:** The archive's combat playbook gives Eviscerate the condition "5 combo points, target will die before Rupture pays off or target is bleed-immune" -- Rupture is not in this file, so Eviscerate is the spec's only dump and the second clause is always satisfied.
